mission.title: etcd: Restore etcd snapshot on a kubeadm control plane
mission.description: After etcd data loss or corruption, kube-apiserver fails with `etcdserver: mvcc: database space exceeded` or `Unable to connect to the server: EOF`, and etcd logs `database corrupted`. Restore from a snapshot taken with etcdctl.

steps.title: Verify the snapshot is valid
steps.description:
```bash
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdutl snapshot status /var/backups/etcd-snapshot.db -w table
```

Shows hash, revision, total keys and size. Older versions: `etcdctl snapshot status`.

steps.title: Stop static control plane pods
steps.description:
```bash
sudo mkdir -p /etc/kubernetes/manifests-stopped
sudo mv /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml /etc/kubernetes/manifests-stopped/
sudo crictl ps | grep -E 'etcd|kube-apiserver'
```

steps.title: Restore snapshot into a new data dir
steps.description:
```bash
sudo mv /var/lib/etcd /var/lib/etcd.broken
sudo etcdutl snapshot restore /var/backups/etcd-snapshot.db --data-dir /var/lib/etcd
```

For multi-member clusters, pass `--name`, `--initial-cluster`, `--initial-advertise-peer-urls` on each control plane node using the same snapshot.

steps.title: Restart control plane and check etcd health
steps.description:
```bash
sudo mv /etc/kubernetes/manifests-stopped/*.yaml /etc/kubernetes/manifests/
sudo ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key endpoint health
```

steps.title: Verify cluster state
steps.description:
```bash
kubectl get nodes
kubectl get pods -A | grep -v Running
```

Restart kubelet on workers if pods are stale: `sudo systemctl restart kubelet`.

resolution.summary: The root cause is that the etcd data directory was corrupted or exceeded its quota, so the API server could not read cluster state. Restoring a snapshot into a fresh data dir works because it rebuilds the bbolt database and a new cluster identity from consistent data, while stopping static pods first prevents writes during the restore.

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with etcd available or the issue environment reproducible.
